Section 104 of the BSA 2023 defines the 'Burden of proof', stating that he who asserts must prove.

Additional info: This establishes the initial obligation of a party to prove their case.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 105 of the BSA 2023, on whom does the burden of proof in a suit or proceeding lie?
optionA: The person who would fail if no evidence at all were given on either side
explanation:
Section 105 dictates that the burden of proof lies on that person who would fail if no evidence at all were given on either side.

Additional info: This helps determine which party must initiate the evidentiary process.

subject: Law
question: When a person is accused of an offence, the burden of proving the existence of circumstances bringing the case within General Exceptions of the BNS 2023 lies on whom?
explanation:
Section 108 of the BSA 2023 explicitly places the burden of proving General Exceptions on the accused person.

Additional info: The Court shall presume the absence of such circumstances until proven otherwise.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 110 of the BSA 2023, what is the burden regarding a person shown to have been alive within thirty years?
optionA: The burden to prove they are dead is on the person who affirms it
optionB: The burden to prove they are alive is on the person who affirms it
optionC: They are legally presumed dead after 15 years
explanation:
Section 110 places the burden of proving that a person is dead on the person who affirms it, if the person was known to be alive within the last 30 years.

Additional info: This establishes a presumption of continuity of life for 30 years.

subject: Law
question: Section 111 of the BSA 2023 shifts the burden of proof if a person has not been heard of for how many years?
explanation:
Section 111 states that if a person has not been heard of for seven years by those who would naturally have heard of him, the burden of proving he is alive shifts to the person affirming it.

Additional info: This is commonly known as the presumption of civil death.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 116 of the BSA 2023, the birth of a child during the continuance of a valid marriage is considered what kind of proof of legitimacy?
explanation:
Section 116 makes the birth of a child during a valid marriage (or within 280 days of its dissolution, the mother remaining unmarried) conclusive proof of legitimacy.

Additional info: The only exception is if it can be shown that the parties had no access to each other.

subject: Law
question: Which section of the BSA 2023 deals specifically with the presumption as to dowry death?
explanation:
Section 118 of the BSA 2023 mandates that the Court shall presume dowry death if it is shown that soon before her death, the woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment for dowry.

Additional info: This section works in tandem with Section 80 of the BNS 2023.

subject: Law
question: The legal principle preventing a person from denying the truth of a statement they previously intentionally caused another to believe, is codified as 'Estoppel' under which section of the BSA 2023?
explanation:
Section 121 defines the doctrine of Estoppel.

Additional info: It stops a person from contradicting their own previous declarations or acts to the detriment of someone who relied on them.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 124 of the BSA 2023, who is competent to testify in a Court of law?
optionB: All persons, unless the Court considers they cannot understand the questions or give rational answers
optionC: Only persons without any criminal record
explanation:
Section 124 states that all persons shall be competent to testify unless prevented by tender years, extreme old age, disease, or similar cause from understanding questions or giving rational answers.

Additional info: Even a lunatic can testify if they can understand the questions.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 125 of the BSA 2023, if a witness is unable to communicate verbally, how can they give their evidence?
optionC: In any other manner they can make it intelligible, such as by writing or signs
optionD: Only by submitting a pre-written affidavit
explanation:
Section 125 allows a witness unable to speak to give evidence in any intelligible manner, like writing or signs, in open Court.

Additional info: Such evidence is still considered oral evidence.

subject: Law
question: Section 128 of the BSA 2023 protects which type of communications from being disclosed without consent?
optionC: Communications during marriage between husband and wife
explanation:
Section 128 provides privilege to communications made during marriage between a husband and wife.

Additional info: They cannot be compelled to disclose such communications except in suits between themselves.

subject: Law
question: Evidence derived from unpublished official records relating to any affairs of State requires the permission of whom to be admitted under Section 129?
optionB: The officer at the head of the department concerned
explanation:
Section 129 dictates that evidence from unpublished official records relating to affairs of State cannot be given without the permission of the head of the department.

Additional info: The departmental head has the discretion to give or withhold such permission.

subject: Law
question: The strict privilege protecting 'Professional communications' between a legal adviser and their client is found in which section of the BSA 2023?
explanation:
Section 132 of the BSA 2023 safeguards professional communications made to a legal adviser in the course of employment.

Additional info: This privilege does not extend to communications made in furtherance of any illegal purpose.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 138 of the BSA 2023, can a witness be excused from answering a relevant question on the ground that the answer will criminate them?
optionC: No, a witness is not excused from answering
optionD: No, unless they are a public servant
explanation:
Section 138 clearly states that a witness shall not be excused from answering a question upon a relevant matter simply because the answer may criminate them.

Additional info: However, such compelled answers cannot subject them to arrest or prosecution, except for giving false evidence.

subject: Law
question: Section 139 of the BSA 2023 declares that an accomplice shall be a competent witness against whom?
explanation:
Section 139 establishes that an accomplice is a competent witness against an accused person.

Additional info: A conviction is not illegal merely because it proceeds upon the uncorroborated testimony of an accomplice, though courts often look for corroboration.

subject: Law
question: What is the minimum number of witnesses required by Section 140 of the BSA 2023 to prove any particular fact?
optionC: One eyewitness and one circumstantial witness
optionD: No particular number of witnesses is required
explanation:
Section 140 explicitly states that no particular number of witnesses shall in any case be required for the proof of any fact.

Additional info: The law focuses on the quality and credibility of the evidence, not the quantity.

subject: Law
question: The order in which witnesses are produced and examined is primarily regulated by what, according to Section 141 of the BSA 2023?
optionB: The law and practice relating to civil and criminal procedure
optionD: The severity of the alleged crime
explanation:
Section 141 specifies that the order of witness production and examination shall be regulated by the procedural laws (like BNSS 2023 and CPC).

Additional info: In the absence of such law, it is at the discretion of the Court.

subject: Law
question: When either party proposes to give evidence of any fact, who decides whether the fact, if proved, would be admissible under Section 142?
explanation:
Section 142 gives the Judge the authority to ask the party proposing evidence how it would be relevant, and to decide on its admissibility.

Additional info: The Judge admits the evidence only if they think that the fact, if proved, would be relevant.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 143 of the BSA 2023, the examination of a witness by the party who calls him is formally known as what?
explanation:
Section 143 defines the examination of a witness by the party who calls him as the 'examination-in-chief'.

Additional info: The subsequent examination by the adverse party is called cross-examination.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 144 of the BSA 2023, if a witness is re-examined, the re-examination must be directed to what?
optionB: The explanation of matters referred to in cross-examination
explanation:
Section 144 restricts re-examination strictly to the explanation of matters referred to in cross-examination.

Additional info: If new matter is introduced (with Court permission) during re-examination, the adverse party may further cross-examine upon that matter.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 145 of the BSA 2023, if a person is summoned merely to produce a document and produces it, does he become a witness who can be cross-examined?
optionB: No, he does not become a witness and cannot be cross-examined unless called as a witness
optionC: Yes, but only regarding the document's authenticity
optionD: Yes, but only by the Court
explanation:
Section 145 clarifies that a person summoned to produce a document does not become a witness by the mere fact that he produces it.

Additional info: He cannot be cross-examined unless and until he is officially called as a witness.

subject: Law
question: Section 147 of the BSA 2023 defines a "leading question" as what?
optionA: A question that leads to a confession
optionB: A question suggesting the answer which the person putting it wishes or expects to receive
optionC: The first question asked in an examination-in-chief
optionD: A question asked directly by the Judge
explanation:
Section 147 defines a leading question as any question suggesting the answer which the person putting it wishes or expects to receive.

Additional info: Leading questions are generally prohibited in examination-in-chief but permitted in cross-examination.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 148 of the BSA 2023, leading questions must NOT be asked (if objected to) during which stages, without the permission of the Court?
explanation:
Section 148 prohibits the use of leading questions during an examination-in-chief, or in a re-examination, if the adverse party objects, unless the Court permits it.

Additional info: The Court typically permits them for introductory or undisputed matters.

subject: Law
question: Which section of the BSA 2023 allows a witness to be cross-examined as to previous statements made by him in writing or reduced into writing, without such writing being shown to him?
explanation:
Section 151 permits cross-examination on previous written statements without showing them to the witness.

Additional info: However, if the statement is to be used to contradict the witness, his attention must be drawn to those parts before proving the writing.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 152 of the BSA 2023, during cross-examination, questions may be put to a witness to test their veracity or discover who they are, even if the answer might do what?
optionB: Directly criminate them or expose them to a penalty
explanation:
Section 152 allows questions in cross-examination to shake the witness's credit by injuring their character, even if the answer might tend directly or indirectly to criminate them.

Additional info: This is vital for effectively testing the reliability of the witness.

subject: Law
question: The Court is mandated to forbid any questions or inquiries which it regards as indecent or scandalous, under which section of the BSA 2023?
explanation:
Section 157 strictly empowers and mandates the Court to forbid indecent and scandalous questions.

Additional info: The only exception is if such questions relate to facts in issue or matters necessary to determine true facts in issue.

subject: Law
question: Which section of the BSA 2023 allows the Court to permit a party who calls a witness to put any questions to him which might be put in cross-examination by the adverse party (often referred to as 'hostile witness' provision)?
explanation:
Section 160 gives the Court the discretion to allow a party to cross-examine their own witness.

Additional info: This is typically used when the witness turns 'hostile' and does not support the case of the party who called them.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 161 of the BSA 2023, the credit of a witness may be impeached by the adverse party by proving what?
optionB: That the witness is a relative of the accused
optionC: That the witness has been bribed or has received any other corrupt inducement to give his evidence
optionD: That the witness has not sworn an oath
explanation:
Section 161 specifies the methods for impeaching a witness's credit, which includes proving that the witness has been bribed or accepted a corrupt inducement.

Additional info: It also allows calling independent persons to testify that the witness is unworthy of credit.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 165 of the BSA 2023, while under examination, a witness may refresh his memory by referring to any writing made by himself at what time?
optionA: At any time before the trial
optionB: At the time of the transaction concerning which he is questioned, or so soon afterwards that the Court considers it fresh in his memory
optionC: Only while standing in the witness box
optionD: Only after the Court grants a formal adjournment
explanation:
Section 165 allows a witness to refresh their memory using documents written by them at the time of the event or very shortly thereafter.

Additional info: A witness can also use documents made by someone else, if they read it within that timeframe and knew it to be correct.

subject: Law
question: Which specific section of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 expressly provides for the 'Repeal and savings' of previous evidentiary laws?
explanation:
"Section 170 of the BSA 2023 contains the provisions for 'Repeal and savings'.

Additional info: This is the concluding section of the Act."

subject: Law
question: According to Article 1 of the Indian Constitution, what shall India, that is Bharat, be?
explanation:
Article 1(1) explicitly states that India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.

Additional info: The States and their territories are specified in the First Schedule.

subject: Law
question: Under Article 11 of the Constitution, who is empowered to regulate the right of citizenship by law?
explanation:
Article 11 grants Parliament the power to make any provision with respect to the acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters relating to citizenship.

Additional info: This overrides anything in the preceding provisions of Part II regarding citizenship rights.

subject: Law
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution defines 'the State' for the purposes of Part III (Fundamental Rights)?
explanation:
Article 12 defines 'the State' to include the Government and Parliament of India, the Government and Legislature of each State, and all local or other authorities within the territory of India.

Additional info: This definition is crucial because Fundamental Rights are primarily guaranteed against actions of the State.

subject: Law
question:
Article 15(1) prohibits the State from discriminating against any citizen on grounds only of

which of the following?
optionA: Religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth
optionB: Religion, race, language, sex, place of birth
optionC: Religion, caste, wealth, sex, place of birth
explanation:
Article 15(1) states that the State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them.

Additional info: Special provisions can still be made for women, children, and socially and educationally backward classes under subsequent clauses.

subject: Law
question: Which fundamental right was expanded by the Supreme Court in the Maneka Gandhi case to collectively test against guarantees of fairness and reasonableness?
explanation:
In the Maneka Gandhi case, the Supreme Court held that governmental restraints on 'personal liberty' under Article 21 should collectively be tested against the guarantees of fairness and reasonableness.

Additional info: This decision incorporated the guarantee of 'substantive due process' into the language of Article 21.

subject: Law
question: According to Article 37, the Directive Principles of State Policy contained in Part IV of the Constitution are:
explanation:
Article 37 explicitly states that the provisions contained in Part IV shall not be enforceable by any court.

Additional info: However, the principles therein laid down are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country, and it is the duty of the State to apply them.

subject: Law
question: Article 50 of the Constitution directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from which branch in the public services?
explanation:
Article 50 mandates that the State shall take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.

Additional info: This Directive Principle is aimed at ensuring the independence and impartiality of the judicial system.

subject: Law
question: How many members having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service can the President nominate to the Council of States?
explanation:
Article 80(1)(a) read with Article 80(3) states that twelve members shall be nominated by the President having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service.

Additional info: The Council of States shall consist of not more than two hundred and thirty-eight representatives of the States and Union territories besides these twelve.

subject: Law
question: Under Article 110 of the Constitution, if any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, whose decision thereon shall be final?
optionC: The Speaker of the House of the People
optionD: The Chairman of the Council of States
explanation:
Article 110(3) provides that if any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, the decision of the Speaker of the House of the People thereon shall be final.

Additional info: The Speaker's certificate must be endorsed on the Money Bill when transmitted to the Council of States.

subject: Law
question: Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court of India. According to the Constitution, who appoints the Judges of the Supreme Court?
explanation:
Article 124 states that there shall be a Supreme Court of India and outlines its establishment, with the President appointing its judges.

Additional info: The President appoints the Chief Justice and other Judges by warrant under his hand and seal.

subject: Law
question: Under Article 148, who is responsible for the audit of the accounts of the Union and of the States?
optionC: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
explanation:
Article 148 establishes the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, who performs duties and exercises powers in relation to the accounts of the Union and the States under Article 149.

Additional info: The reports of the CAG relating to the accounts of the Union are submitted to the President.

subject: Law
question: The power of the Governor to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment is granted under which Article?
explanation:
Article 161 empowers the Governor of a State to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment or commute the sentence of any person.

Additional info: This power is exercised for any offence against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the State extends.

subject: Law
question: What is the minimum and maximum number of members a State Legislative Assembly can consist of according to Article 170(1)?
optionA: Not more than four hundred and not less than fifty
optionB: Not more than five hundred and not less than sixty
optionC: Not more than five hundred and fifty and not less than sixty
optionD: Not more than six hundred and not less than forty
explanation:
Article 170(1) dictates that the Legislative Assembly of each State shall consist of not more than five hundred, and not less than sixty, members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies.

Additional info: This composition is subject to the provisions of Article 333.

subject: Law
question:
Article 246A was inserted to make special provisions with respect to

which of the following?
explanation:
Article 246A provides special provision with respect to goods and services tax, granting Parliament and the Legislature of every State the power to make laws with respect to GST.

Additional info: It was inserted by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016.

subject: Law
question: Under Article 265 of the Constitution, what is the fundamental condition for the levy or collection of any tax?
optionA: It must be approved by the Finance Commission
optionB: It must be supported by a Presidential ordinance
optionC: It must be by authority of law
optionD: It must be approved by the Supreme Court
explanation:
Article 265 explicitly states: 'No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.'

Additional info: This rule ensures that the executive cannot impose or gather taxes without proper legislative sanction.

subject: Law
question: The President is required to constitute a Finance Commission within two years from the commencement of the Constitution and thereafter every fifth year under which Article?
explanation:
Article 280 mandates the President to constitute a Finance Commission consisting of a Chairman and four other members.

Additional info: The Commission makes recommendations regarding the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Union and States.

subject: Law
question: Under Article 312, Parliament may by law provide for the creation of one or more all-India services if which house passes a resolution declaring it necessary in the national interest?
explanation:
Article 312 requires the Council of States to pass a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting to create new all-India services.

Additional info: This provision includes the power to create an all-India judicial service.

subject: Law
question: According to Article 324, the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections shall be vested in:
explanation:
Article 324 vests the complete authority of superintendence, direction, and control of elections in an independent Election Commission.

Additional info: This independent authority is fundamental for ensuring free and fair democratic elections.

subject: Law
question: The President can proclaim a National Emergency under Article 352 if the security of India is threatened by war, external aggression, or what other ground?
explanation:
Article 352 allows the President to issue a Proclamation of Emergency due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.

Additional info: The ground of 'internal disturbance' was replaced by 'armed rebellion' through the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act.

subject: Law
question: A Proclamation of Emergency under Article 352 must be approved by resolutions of both Houses of Parliament within what timeframe from its issue?
explanation:
Article 352(4) dictates that every Proclamation shall cease to operate at the expiration of one month unless it has been approved by resolutions of both Houses of Parliament.

Additional info: If the Lok Sabha is dissolved, special provisions apply involving the Rajya Sabha's approval.

subject: Law
question: Which Article provides for the assumption of functions of the State Government by the President in case of a failure of constitutional machinery in a State (President's Rule)?
explanation:
Article 356 empowers the President to issue a Proclamation if he is satisfied that the State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.

Additional info: This action is commonly referred to as invoking President's Rule or a State Emergency.

subject: Law
question: Under Article 360, the President can proclaim a Financial Emergency if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen whereby the financial stability or credit of India is:
explanation:
Article 360(1) allows the President to declare a Financial Emergency if the financial stability or credit of India or of any part of the territory thereof is threatened.

Additional info: During this emergency, the Union can give financial directions to states, including reducing salaries.

subject: Law
question: Which landmark Supreme Court case established the 'Basic Structure' doctrine, holding that Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution?
optionC: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
explanation:
In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), the Supreme Court ruled that while Parliament can amend the Constitution, it cannot alter its 'basic structure'.

Additional info: This doctrine protects fundamental constitutional principles like judicial review and secularism from being destroyed by amendments.

subject: Law
question: Article 368 provides that an amendment to certain federal provisions requires, in addition to a special majority of Parliament, ratification by what proportion of the State Legislatures?
explanation:
According to Article 368, if an amendment seeks to change specific federal provisions, it requires ratification by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States.

Additional info: The ratification must be done by a simple majority before the Bill is presented to the President.

subject: Law
question: The Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, which contains provisions as to disqualification on the ground of defection, applies to members of:
optionA: Only the House of the People
optionC: Both Houses of Parliament and State Legislatures
explanation:
The Tenth Schedule applies to members of a 'House', which is explicitly defined to include both Houses of Parliament and the State Legislatures.

Additional info: A member can be disqualified if they voluntarily give up their party membership or defy party whips.

subject: Law
question:
According to the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976,

which of the following was introduced to emphasize the responsibilities of citizens alongside their rights?
explanation:
The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 introduced Fundamental Duties for Indian citizens.

Additional info: This was meant to emphasize the responsibilities of citizens alongside their fundamental rights.

subject: Law
question: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution contains exactly how many words?
explanation:
The Preamble contains exactly 73 words, outlining the fundamental principles that guide the Indian Constitution.

Additional info: The Supreme Court has affirmed that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.

subject: Law
question: In the Minerva Mills Case (1980), the Supreme Court emphasized the power of the courts to determine the legality of legislative actions. What is this power called?
explanation:
In the Minerva Mills Case, the Supreme Court observed that the Constitution created an independent judiciary vested with the power of judicial review to determine the validity of legislation.

Additional info: Judicial review acts as a tool to check the constitutionality of legislative and executive actions.

subject: Law
question: Which Schedule of the Constitution deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes (excluding certain North-Eastern states)?
explanation:
The Fifth Schedule contains provisions as to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.

Additional info: The Sixth Schedule specifically deals with tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.

subject: Law
question: The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution distributes legislative powers. Which list gives Parliament exclusive power to make laws?
explanation:
Article 246(1) gives Parliament exclusive power to make laws with respect to any of the matters enumerated in List I (Union List) in the Seventh Schedule.

Additional info: Subjects like Defence, Foreign Affairs, and Atomic Energy fall exclusively under the Union List.

subject: Science & Technology
question: SpudCell, recently seen in the news, is best described as:
optionB: A synthetic cell assembled using the bottom-up approach
explanation: SpudCell is a laboratory-built synthetic cell created through the bottom-up synthetic biology approach using non-living molecular components.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes SpudCell from genetically modified organisms (GMOs)?
optionA: GMOs are non-living while SpudCell is living
optionC: GMOs modify existing organisms, whereas SpudCell is assembled from non-living molecular components
explanation: GMOs modify existing organisms, whereas SpudCell is assembled from carefully selected non-living molecular components.

subject: Science & Technology
question:
Consider the following statements regarding SpudCell:

1. It depends on externally supplied molecular machinery.
2. It requires controlled laboratory conditions.
3. It possesses fully independent metabolism.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. SpudCell is not fully autonomous and lacks independent metabolism.

subject: Science & Technology
question: SpudCell is associated with which one of the following?
explanation: SpudCell is one of the most advanced examples of bottom-up synthetic biology.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following best describes the significance of SpudCell?
optionB: It demonstrates that several essential cellular processes can be integrated within a synthetic system
optionC: It is a commercially available medical technology
optionD: It proves scientists have created fully autonomous artificial life
explanation: The significance of SpudCell lies in integrating feeding, growth, genome replication and cell division within a synthetic cell.

subject: Law
question: Section 9 of the BSA 2023 makes facts not otherwise relevant become relevant if they are highly probable/improbable or if they are what?
optionA: Inconsistent with any fact in issue or relevant fact
explanation:
Section 9(1) states that facts not otherwise relevant are relevant if they are inconsistent with any fact in issue or relevant fact.

Additional info: This forms the statutory basis for the plea of 'alibi' (being elsewhere).

subject: Law
question: Under Section 2(1)(e) of the BSA 2023, 'oral evidence' includes all statements which the Court permits or requires to be made before it by witnesses, including statements given in what manner?
explanation:
Section 2(1)(e)(i) expands oral evidence to include all statements 'including statements given electronically' made before the Court by witnesses.

Additional info: This legally recognizes testimonies via video conferencing and other electronic means.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 34 of the BSA 2023, the existence of a previous judgment which by law prevents any Court from holding a trial is considered what kind of fact?
explanation:
Section 34 makes the existence of any judgment, order or decree which prevents a Court from taking cognizance or holding a trial a relevant fact.

Additional info: This is the evidentiary implementation of the Res Judicata principle.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 15 of the BSA 2023, an 'admission' is a statement which suggests an inference as to any fact in issue or relevant fact, and can be in which forms?
optionC: Oral, documentary or contained in electronic form
explanation:
Section 15 defines an admission broadly as a statement, oral or documentary or contained in electronic form, which suggests any inference.

Additional info: The definition expressly accommodates modern digital communications.

subject: Law
question: When the BSA 2023 declares that one fact is 'conclusive proof' of another, what is the Court required to do upon proof of the one fact?
optionC: Regard the other as proved and not allow evidence to disprove it
explanation:
Section 2(1)(b) defines 'conclusive proof' meaning the Court shall regard the other fact as proved and shall not allow evidence to be given for the purpose of disproving it.

Additional info: This creates an irrebuttable presumption of law.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 39(1) of the BSA 2023, persons specially skilled in foreign law, science, art, or identity of handwriting/finger impressions are called what?
explanation:
Section 39(1) defines such specially skilled persons whose opinions are relevant upon those specific points as 'experts'.

Additional info: The BSA 2023 explicitly adds 'or any other field' to the traditional list of expert topics.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 6(1) of the BSA 2023, any fact is relevant which shows or constitutes what for any fact in issue or relevant fact?
explanation:
Section 6(1) explicitly states that any fact is relevant which shows or constitutes a motive or preparation for any fact in issue or relevant fact.

Additional info: For example, procuring poison before a murder is relevant as preparation.

subject: Law
question: Section 23(1) of the BSA 2023 lays down a strict rule regarding confessions made to whom?
explanation:
Section 23(1) unequivocally states: 'No confession made to a police officer shall be proved as against a person accused of any offence.'

Additional info: This aims to prevent coerced or tortured confessions during police custody.

subject: Law
question: Where the question is as to the existence of any right or custom, Section 11(a) of the BSA 2023 makes relevant any transaction by which the right or custom was:
optionB: Created, claimed, modified, recognised, asserted or denied
explanation:
Under Section 11(a), any transaction by which the right or custom in question was created, claimed, modified, recognised, asserted or denied is relevant.

Additional info: Section 11(b) also makes particular instances of such claims or exercises relevant.

subject: Law
question: Section 25 of the BSA 2023 declares that admissions are NOT conclusive proof of the matters admitted, but they may operate as what?
explanation:
Section 25 states that while admissions are not conclusive proof, they may operate as estoppels under the provisions of the Adhiniyam.

Additional info: This means a party may be prevented from denying the truth of their previous admission if another party acted upon it.

subject: Law
question: According to Explanation 1 of Section 6 of the BSA 2023, the word 'conduct' does NOT include statements, UNLESS those statements do what?
optionB: Accompany and explain acts other than statements
explanation:
Explanation 1 clarifies that 'conduct' does not include statements, unless those statements accompany and explain acts other than statements.

Additional info: However, this explanation does not affect the relevancy of statements under other sections.

subject: Law
question:
According to Section 1 of the BSA 2023, the Adhiniyam applies to all judicial proceedings in or before any Court, but does NOT apply to

which of the following?
explanation:
Section 1(2) explicitly states that the Act applies to all judicial proceedings in or before any Court, including Courts-martial, but not to affidavits presented to any Court or officer, nor to proceedings before an arbitrator.

Additional info: Affidavits are generally governed by specific procedural rules of the courts rather than the strict rules of evidence.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 41(1) of the BSA 2023, when the Court has to form an opinion as to the person by whom a document was written, whose opinion is relevant?
optionB: Any person acquainted with the handwriting of that person
explanation:
Section 41(1) makes relevant the opinion of any person acquainted with the handwriting of the person by whom it is supposed to be written or signed.

Additional info: The explanation details that seeing the person write or receiving habitual correspondence makes one 'acquainted'.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 2(1)(h) of the BSA 2023, whenever it is provided that the Court 'may presume' a fact, the Court may either regard such fact as proved unless disproved, or do what?
optionD: Refer it to a larger bench
explanation:
Under the definition of 'may presume', the Court has the discretion to either regard the fact as proved until disproved, or it may call for proof of it.

Additional info: This gives the Court flexibility based on the circumstances of each individual case.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 28 of the BSA 2023, entries in books of account regularly kept in the course of business are relevant, but are they alone sufficient to charge a person with liability?
optionB: Yes, if certified by an auditor
optionC: No, they shall not alone be sufficient evidence
explanation:
Section 28 explicitly states that such statements shall not alone be sufficient evidence to charge any person with liability.

Additional info: Independent corroborative evidence is required to prove the actual transaction.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 8 of the BSA 2023, anything said, done or written by a conspirator in reference to their common intention is a relevant fact against each conspirator AFTER what specific point in time?
optionB: After the time when such intention was first entertained by any of them
explanation:
Section 8 makes acts and statements of conspirators relevant after the time when such intention was first entertained by any one of them.

Additional info: This is relevant to prove both the existence of the conspiracy and a person's complicity in it.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 35(2) of the BSA 2023, a final judgment of a competent Court in the exercise of probate or matrimonial jurisdiction is what kind of proof of the legal character it confers?
explanation:
Section 35(2) dictates that such a judgment, order or decree is conclusive proof that any legal character which it confers accrued at that time.

Additional info: These are commonly referred to as judgments in rem.

subject: Law
question: Section 4 of the BSA 2023 makes facts relevant if they form part of the same transaction, whether they occurred at the same time and place or at:
optionC: Only different places but same time
optionD: Only same place but different times
explanation:
Section 4 states that facts forming part of the same transaction are relevant, whether they occurred at the same time and place or at different times and places.

Additional info: This is traditionally known as the doctrine of res gestae.

subject: Law
question: To make a fact relevant as showing the existence of a relevant state of mind under Section 12, Explanation 1 requires that it must show the state of mind exists how?
optionA: In reference to the particular matter in question
explanation:
Explanation 1 to Section 12 mandates that the fact must show that the state of mind exists, not generally, but in reference to the particular matter in question.

Additional info: A general disposition or habit is not sufficient.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 24 of the BSA 2023, when multiple persons are tried jointly for the same offence, and a confession by one affects himself and another, what can the Court do?
optionB: It cannot use it against the other person
optionC: It may take into consideration such confession against the other person
optionD: Send the case to a higher court
explanation:
Section 24 allows the Court to take into consideration such a confession against the co-accused as well as against the maker.

Additional info: An explanation clarifies that a trial held in the absence of an absconding accused is deemed a joint trial.

subject: Law
question: Section 30 of the BSA 2023 makes statements of facts relevant if they are made in published maps or charts generally offered for what?
explanation:
Statements of facts in published maps or charts generally offered for public sale, or maps made under the authority of the Government, are themselves relevant facts.

Additional info: Their public nature gives them a presumption of general accuracy.

subject: Law
question: Which of the following facts are made relevant under Section 5 of the BSA 2023?
optionA: Facts which are occasion, cause or effect of relevant facts
optionC: Facts totally unconnected to the issue
explanation:
Section 5 makes facts relevant if they are the occasion, cause or effect, immediate or otherwise, of relevant facts, or facts in issue.

Additional info: It also includes facts which afforded an opportunity for the occurrence.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 39(2) of the BSA 2023, the opinion of the Examiner of Electronic Evidence (referred to in Sec 79A of the IT Act, 2000) is a relevant fact, and such examiner shall be considered a what?
explanation:
The Explanation to Section 39(2) explicitly states: 'For the purposes of this sub-section, an Examiner of Electronic Evidence shall be an expert.'

Additional info: This ensures digital evidence is analyzed and validated by recognized experts.

subject: Law
question: In suits in which damages are claimed, Section 10 of the BSA 2023 dictates that any fact is relevant if it enables the Court to determine what?
optionB: The amount of damages which ought to be awarded
explanation:
Section 10 clearly states that any fact which will enable the Court to determine the amount of damages which ought to be awarded is relevant.

Additional info: This helps quantify the financial impact of the wrong committed.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 26(a) of the BSA 2023, a statement by a person who is dead is relevant if it relates to what?
explanation:
Section 26(a) makes a statement relevant if it is made by a person as to the cause of his death, or the circumstances of the transaction which resulted in his death.

Additional info: This is legally recognized as a dying declaration.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 2(1)(a) of the BSA 2023, the definition of 'Court' includes all Judges, Magistrates, and persons legally authorised to take evidence, EXCEPT whom?
explanation:
The definition of 'Court' under Section 2(1)(a) expressly excludes arbitrators.

Additional info: Proceedings before arbitrators are intended to be flexible and are guided by principles of natural justice rather than strict evidentiary laws.

subject: Law
question: Section 38 of the BSA 2023 allows any party to a suit to show that a judgment proved by the adverse party was delivered by an incompetent Court or was obtained by what?
explanation:
Section 38 permits a party to show that a relevant judgment, order or decree was delivered by a Court not competent to deliver it, or was obtained by fraud or collusion.

Additional info: Fraud vitiates all solemn acts, including judgments.

subject: Law
question:
The definition of 'document' in Section 2(1)(d) of the BSA 2023 specifically includes

which of the following modern formats?
explanation:
The definition of 'document' explicitly includes electronic and digital records.

Additional info: The illustrations clearly mention emails, server logs, smartphone documents, websites, locational evidence, and voice mail messages as documents.

subject: Law
question: When there is a question whether a particular act was done, Section 14 makes relevant the existence of what?
optionB: Any course of business according to which it naturally would have been done
explanation:
Section 14 dictates that the existence of any course of business, according to which an act naturally would have been done, is a relevant fact.

Additional info: For example, the ordinary routine of posting and delivering letters.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 21 of the BSA 2023, an admission in a civil case is NOT relevant if it is made upon what condition?
optionA: An express condition that evidence of it is not to be given
optionB: A condition that it is recorded
explanation:
Section 21 states that no admission is relevant in civil cases if made upon an express condition that evidence of it is not to be given, or if the Court infers parties agreed not to give evidence of it.

Additional info: This protects statements made 'without prejudice' during settlement negotiations.

subject: Law
question: Section 74 of the BSA 2023 classifies documents forming the acts or records of the acts of sovereign authority and official bodies as what?
explanation:
Section 74(1) categorizes documents forming the acts or records of the sovereign authority, official bodies, and public officers as 'public documents'.

Additional info: All other documents are classified as private documents under sub-section (2).

subject: Law
question: Section 49 of the BSA 2023 states that in criminal proceedings, the previous bad character of the accused is irrelevant UNLESS what happens?
optionA: The crime is punishable by death
optionB: Evidence has been given that he has a good character
explanation:
Section 49 makes previous bad character irrelevant, unless evidence has been given that he has a good character, in which case it becomes relevant in reply.

Additional info: A previous conviction is also relevant as evidence of bad character.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 98 of the BSA 2023, when language in a document is plain in itself but unmeaning in reference to existing facts (Latent Ambiguity), can evidence be given to show its peculiar sense?
explanation:
Section 98 allows evidence to be given to show that the plain language was used in a peculiar sense when it applies to existing facts.

Additional info: For example, a deed selling 'my house in Kolkata' when the seller only has a house in Howrah, of which the buyer took possession.

subject: Law
question: Section 57 of the BSA 2023 defines 'Primary evidence' primarily as what?
optionB: The document itself produced for the inspection of the Court
optionC: An oral account by an eyewitness
explanation:
Section 57 defines primary evidence as the document itself produced for the inspection of the Court.

Additional info: It is the best evidence rule in practice.

subject: Law
question: Section 85 of the BSA 2023 requires the Court to presume what regarding every electronic record purporting to be an agreement containing the electronic/digital signature of the parties?
optionC: That it was so concluded by affixing those signatures
explanation:
Section 85 dictates that the Court shall presume that the agreement was so concluded by the parties affixing their electronic or digital signature.

Additional info: This gives legal certainty to electronic contracts.

subject: Law
question: Section 47 of the BSA 2023 provides that in criminal proceedings, the fact that the person accused is of a good character is legally considered:
explanation:
Section 47 expressly provides that in criminal proceedings the fact that the person accused is of a good character is relevant.

Additional info: This helps to establish that it is unlikely the accused committed the alleged crime.

subject: Law
question: Section 61 of the BSA 2023 ensures that nothing in the Adhiniyam shall deny the admissibility of a record merely on the ground that it is a what?
explanation:
Section 61 explicitly protects the admissibility of electronic or digital records, stating they shall have the same legal effect, validity, and enforceability as other documents, subject to Section 63.

Additional info: This modernizes the evidence framework.

subject: Law
question: Section 100 of the BSA 2023 deals with language that applies partly to one set of facts and partly to another, but correctly to neither. Can evidence be given to show which it meant to apply to?
optionC: Only if the document is 30 years old
optionD: Only if it is a public document
explanation:
Section 100 states that evidence may be given to show to which of the two sets of facts it was meant to apply.

Additional info: This resolves situations where descriptions are partially inaccurate for multiple potential subjects.

subject: Law
question: Which of the following is specifically included in the definition of 'Secondary evidence' under Section 58 of the BSA 2023?
explanation:
Section 58 lists 'certified copies given under the provisions hereinafter contained' as the first category of secondary evidence.

Additional info: It also includes copies made by mechanical processes, oral accounts, and counterparts against non-executing parties.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 92 of the BSA 2023, if a document purporting to be how many years old is produced from proper custody, the Court may presume its signature and execution?
explanation:
Section 92 provides a presumption of due execution and handwriting for documents purporting or proved to be thirty years old, if produced from proper custody.

Additional info: This is a rule of convenience for ancient documents where witnesses are likely dead.

subject: Law
question: Section 55 of the BSA 2023 mandates that oral evidence shall, in all cases whatever, be what?
explanation:
Section 55 lays down the fundamental rule that 'Oral evidence shall, in all cases whatever, be direct'.

Additional info: This means if it refers to a fact which could be seen, it must be the evidence of a witness who says he saw it.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 75 of the BSA 2023, what must a public officer give to a person who has a right to inspect a public document, on demand and payment of legal fees?
explanation:
Section 75 mandates the public officer to give a copy together with a certificate written at the foot that it is a true copy, dated, signed, and sealed.

Additional info: Such copies so certified shall be called certified copies.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 46 of the BSA 2023, in civil cases, the fact that the character of any person is such as to render probable or improbable any conduct imputed to him is generally what?
explanation:
Section 46 states that in civil cases such character evidence is irrelevant, except in so far as such character appears from facts otherwise relevant.

Additional info: Civil cases are decided on facts and merits, not on the general character of the parties.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 95 of the BSA 2023, when the terms of a contract have been reduced to a document and proved, what is excluded for the purpose of contradicting or varying its terms?
optionB: Evidence of any oral agreement or statement
explanation:
Section 95 mandates that no evidence of any oral agreement or statement shall be admitted between the parties for the purpose of contradicting, varying, adding to, or subtracting from its terms.

Additional info: This is the core of the parol evidence rule.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 60(c) of the BSA 2023, secondary evidence relating to documents may be given when the original has been what?
explanation:
Section 60(c) allows secondary evidence when the original has been destroyed or lost, or when the party cannot produce it in reasonable time through no default of his own.

Additional info: Any secondary evidence of the contents is admissible in this scenario.

subject: Law
question: Section 103 of the BSA 2023 explicitly saves the provisions of which specific Act relating to the construction of wills from being affected by Chapter VI?
explanation:
Section 103 clearly states: 'Nothing in this Chapter shall be taken to affect any of the provisions of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 as to the construction of wills.'

Additional info: The interpretation of wills continues to be governed by its special statutory framework.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 51 of the BSA 2023, if a Court will take judicial notice of a fact, what is the evidentiary requirement for that fact?
optionA: It must be proved by two witnesses
optionB: It needs to be proved by documentary evidence
optionD: It must be proved by experts
explanation:
Section 51 plainly states: 'No fact of which the Court will take judicial notice need be proved.'

Additional info: This saves the Court's time on universally accepted facts.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 90 of the BSA 2023, the Court may presume that an electronic message forwarded through a mail server corresponds with the message fed into the computer, but shall NOT make any presumption as to what?
optionB: The person by whom such message was sent
explanation:
Section 90 clearly states: 'but the Court shall not make any presumption as to the person by whom such message was sent'.

Additional info: The authorship or identity of the sender must be proved independently.

subject: Law
question: According to Section 65 of the BSA 2023, if a document is alleged to be signed by any person, what must be proved?
optionB: The signature must be proved to be in his handwriting
explanation:
Section 65 requires that the signature or the handwriting of so much of the document as is alleged to be in that person's handwriting must be proved to be in his handwriting.

Additional info: This establishes the authorship and genuineness of the document.

subject: Law
question:
According to Section 101 of the BSA 2023, evidence may be given to show the meaning of

which of the following?
optionB: Illegible characters, obsolete, or technical expressions
explanation:
Section 101 permits evidence to be given to show the meaning of illegible or not commonly intelligible characters, foreign, obsolete, technical, local expressions, and abbreviations.

Additional info: This allows the court to interpret specialized or regional documents accurately.

subject: Law
question:
Under Section 52(1)(a) of the BSA 2023, the Court is mandated to take judicial notice of

which of the following?
optionB: All laws in force in the territory of India
optionD: The financial status of the parties
explanation:
Section 52(1)(a) requires the Court to take judicial notice of all laws in force in the territory of India, including laws having extra-territorial operation.

Additional info: The court also takes judicial notice of international treaties, seals of Courts, and geographic divisions.

subject: Law
question: Section 93 of the BSA 2023 provides a presumption for electronic records regarding the electronic signature if the record is produced from proper custody and is how many years old?
explanation:
Section 93 lowers the threshold for digital forensics, allowing the Court to presume the electronic signature was affixed by the authorized person if the electronic record is five years old.

Additional info: It must be produced from proper custody.

subject: Law
question: Under Explanation 1 to Section 57, where a document is executed in several parts, each part is considered what kind of evidence?
explanation:
Explanation 1 to Section 57 states that where a document is executed in several parts, each part is primary evidence of the document.

Additional info: The same applies when executed in counterparts against the parties executing it.

subject: Law
question: Before secondary evidence can be given of a document in the possession of the adverse party, Section 64 of the BSA 2023 generally requires the proposing party to give what?
explanation:
Section 64 mandates that secondary evidence shall not be given unless the party has previously given to the adverse party such notice to produce it as is prescribed by law.

Additional info: There are exceptions, such as when the document to be proved is itself a notice.

subject: Law
question: Section 96 of the BSA 2023 states that when language in a document is, on its face, ambiguous or defective (Patent Ambiguity), can evidence be given to show its meaning or supply defects?
optionD: Yes, if it is oral evidence
explanation:
Section 96 dictates that evidence may not be given of facts which would show its meaning or supply its defects.

Additional info: For example, a contract selling a horse for '1 lakh or 1.5 lakhs' cannot be cured by oral evidence; it is void.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 48 of the BSA 2023, in a prosecution for rape or sexual offences under the BNS 2023 where consent is in issue, what evidence regarding the victim is strictly NOT relevant?
optionC: Their character or previous sexual experience
explanation:
Section 48 explicitly bars evidence of the character of the victim or of such person's previous sexual experience with any person on the issue of consent or quality of consent.

Additional info: This prevents the victim from being subjected to character assassination during trials.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 78(1) of the BSA 2023, what shall the Court presume regarding every document purporting to be a certificate or certified copy?
explanation:
Section 78(1) states that the Court shall presume to be genuine every document purporting to be a certificate or certified copy which is by law declared to be admissible.

Additional info: It must purport to be duly certified by an authorized officer.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 67 of the BSA 2023, if a document is required by law to be attested, it shall not be used as evidence until what occurs?
optionA: It is published in the Gazette
optionB: At least one attesting witness has been called to prove its execution
explanation:
Section 67 strictly requires that at least one attesting witness must be called for the purpose of proving its execution, if an attesting witness is alive and subject to the court's process.

Additional info: An exception exists for registered documents (other than wills) unless execution is specifically denied.

subject: Law
question:
According to Section 56 of the BSA 2023, the contents of documents may be proved by

which of the following?
explanation:
Section 56 clearly states: 'The contents of documents may be proved either by primary or by secondary evidence.'

Additional info: The general rule is primary evidence, while secondary evidence is admissible only under specific statutory exceptions.

subject: Law
question: Under Section 63(1) of the BSA 2023, information contained in an electronic record which is printed or stored is deemed to be a document and admissible without further proof of the original, provided what?
optionA: It is signed by a judge
optionB: It satisfies the conditions mentioned in Section 63
explanation:
Section 63(1) deems a computer output to be a document and admissible without further proof of the original, IF the conditions mentioned in the section are satisfied.

Additional info: This includes conditions about the regular functioning of the computer and a supporting certificate.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: What is the total estimated outlay for the Union Budget 2026-27?
explanation: The total estimated outlay for the financial year 2026-27 is ₹53.47 lakh crore. For the first time in India's history, this budget was presented on a Sunday, marking Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's 9th consecutive budget presentation.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: What is the Fiscal Deficit target set for 2026-27 in the Union Budget?
explanation: The Fiscal Deficit target for 2026-27 is set at 4.3% of the GDP. Alongside this, the government has introduced a new scheme aimed at stabilizing the overall debt-to-GDP ratio at 50% (±1%) by the year 2030-31.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: How much amount has been allocated for Capital Expenditure (Capex) in the Union Budget 2026-27?
explanation: A record allocation of ₹12.2 lakh crore has been made for Capital Expenditure. This is a significant increase from the previous year's ₹11.21 lakh crore, aimed at accelerating economic growth through strategic infrastructure development.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: What is the budget allocated for the 'Biopharma SHAKTI' scheme?
explanation: The Biopharma SHAKTI scheme has been allocated a budget of ₹10,000 crore. The initiative aims to make India a global hub for Biologics and Biosimilars, and involves upgrading 7 existing NIPERs while opening 3 new ones.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: How much budget has been allocated for Semiconductor Mission 2.0 (ISM 2.0) for 2026-27?
explanation: ₹1,000 crore has been allocated for ISM 2.0. This second phase of the mission explicitly shifts the focus towards high-value manufacturing rather than just basic assembly.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, what is the GDP growth rate for the current financial year (FY26)?
explanation: The GDP growth rate for the current financial year 2025-26 is 7.4%. The projected growth for the upcoming FY27 is slightly lower, ranging between 6.8% and 7.2%, while GVA is estimated at 7.3%.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: Which sector emerged as the fastest-growing with a 9.1% growth rate in the Economic Survey 2025-26?
explanation: The services sector grew at the fastest pace of 9.1%. It acts as the backbone of the economy, followed by the Industry sector at 6.2% and the Agriculture and Allied sector at 3.1%.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: What is the record high of India's Forex Reserves as of January 2026 according to the Economic Survey?
explanation: India's foreign exchange reserves have crossed a massive $701.4 Billion as of January 2026, showcasing a robust and resilient external sector performance.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: What is the estimated Per Capita Net National Income for an average Indian in 2025-26?
explanation: The average annual income of an Indian has reached ₹2.20 lakh for the year 2025-26, reflecting the overall economic expansion.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, how many people filed Income Tax Returns (ITR) in FY25?
explanation: A total of 9.2 crore people filed ITR in the financial year 2025. Interestingly, this coincides with a 9.2% growth in the government's total Revenue Receipts, indicating improved tax compliance.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: What is India's share in global service exports in 2024, as highlighted in the Economic Survey?
explanation: India's share in global service exports has grown significantly from 2% to 4.3%. Driven largely by IT and digital services, India is now the 7th largest service exporter in the world.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question:
The Economic Survey 2025-26 uniquely highlighted

which of the following as a major new threat to economic productivity?
explanation: The survey severely warned against Digital Addiction as a lifestyle threat, linking excessive screen time on electronic gadgets to poor mental health, depression, and reduced productivity.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: What was the total food production in India during the financial year 2024-25?
explanation: Total food production hit a record 3577.3 lakh metric tonnes in FY25. This was a record-breaking harvest, marking an increase of 254.3 lakh metric tonnes from the previous year.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: What is the name of Bihar's first supercomputer to be installed at IIT Patna?
explanation: Param Rudra will be installed as Bihar's first supercomputer at IIT Patna, a move designed to significantly boost the region's advanced technological and research capabilities.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: Who has been appointed as the first Vice-Chancellor of the Jannayak Karpoori Thakur Skill University?
explanation: Deepak Anand has been appointed as the first Vice-Chancellor. The university was established by the state government to provide advanced educational opportunities in skill development for the youth.

subject: Budget and economic survey
question: Where will the state of Bihar's first goat semen station be constructed?
